articles.title: Planning Application Submitted for Nine Houses at Little Nook Farm, Middleton
articles.excerpt: SM Properties has applied to Rochdale Council to demolish Little Nook Farm and construct nine detached homes, with plans for a mix of three, four, and five-bedroom properties.
articles.content_html:
A planning application has been submitted to Rochdale Council by SM Properties to demolish Little Nook Farm, located on Heywood Old Road in Middleton, and replace it with nine detached houses. The proposal includes the construction of seven homes along the Heywood Old Road border and two additional homes towards the back of the site.

The site currently comprises a farmhouse and several outbuildings, with the first records of the farm dating back to 1848. The existing farmhouse was extended between 1968 and 1970. Planning documents indicate that the development aims to remove the existing structures to make way for new residential properties.

According to Groves Town Planning Ltd, the proposed homes will feature three, four, and five bedrooms, catering to a range of family sizes. The application is currently under review by the council, and further details will be made available as the planning process progresses.

Residents and stakeholders may wish to monitor the progress of this application, as it could impact local housing availability and the character of the area. The council will provide updates on the decision-making timeline and any public consultations that may arise.

articles.title: Masdar Launches Battery Storage Project in Rochdale to Power 35,000 Homes Daily
articles.excerpt: Abu Dhabi-based renewable energy company Masdar has commenced operations at a new battery energy storage system in Rochdale, capable of powering 35,000 homes daily as part of its UK investment programme.
articles.content_html:
Abu Dhabi-based renewable energy company Masdar has officially launched its second battery energy storage system (BESS) project in the UK, located in Rochdale. This facility, with a capacity of 35MW/70MWh, is designed to provide enough clean power for approximately 35,000 homes each day, based on two charging and discharging cycles.

The new project is part of Masdar's AED5 billion (£1 billion or $1.36 billion) investment programme aimed at enhancing the UK's energy security and renewable energy infrastructure. The facility will also offer grid-balancing services, responding to fluctuations in electricity supply and demand within milliseconds to support grid stability.

Husain Al Meer, Executive Director, Global Offshore Wind & UK at Masdar, stated, "Beginning commercial operations at our Rochdale facility is a key milestone in our £1 billion commitment to UK battery storage." He emphasised the growing importance of battery storage in maintaining a secure and reliable electricity network as demand for electricity increases and renewable generation expands.

The Rochdale facility follows Masdar's earlier project in Stockport, which began operations in December 2025. Masdar is also developing additional BESS projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff, with a combined capacity of 150MW/300MWh. This expansion aligns with the UK government's Clean Power 2030 Action Plan, which aims for up to 27GW of battery storage capacity by the end of the decade.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Transitions from Microsoft Security to TrendAI in Six Weeks
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has successfully transitioned its security systems from Microsoft to TrendAI within a six-week timeframe, enhancing its cybersecurity measures.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has completed a transition of its cybersecurity systems, moving from Microsoft security solutions to TrendAI in just six weeks. This change aims to bolster the council's digital security and improve its response to potential cyber threats.

The decision to switch to TrendAI was made following a review of the council's existing security measures, which highlighted the need for more advanced protection against evolving cyber risks.

This transition is part of a broader initiative by Rochdale Council to modernise its IT infrastructure and ensure the safety of sensitive data.

As the council integrates TrendAI into its operations, it will continue to assess the effectiveness of the new system.

articles.title: Track Renewal Works on Rochdale Line Affecting Services Until 28 August
articles.excerpt: Track renewal works on the Rochdale line will lead to service changes and a bus replacement service operating between affected stops until 28 August.
articles.content_html:
From Saturday 15 August until Friday 28 August, track renewal works will take place on the Rochdale line, resulting in service changes for commuters and travellers. During this period, a bus replacement service will operate between the affected stops to ensure continued transport options for passengers.

The works coincide with a busy bank holiday weekend in Greater Manchester, which includes events such as Manchester Pride and Manchester United's first home game of the season. Travellers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and allow extra time for travel during this period.

In addition to the track works, there is currently a minor delay on the Airport lines due to an earlier power fault, which was reported on 25 August. Passengers are encouraged to check for updates on the TfGM Travel Alerts page for the latest information on service disruptions.

For those requiring step-free access, the lift at Queens Road tram stop is out of service. Customers needing assistance should contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000 for journey planning support. Lines are open from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and from 8am to 8pm on weekends and bank holidays.

articles.title: Two Women Released on Bail After Three-Year-Old Boy Falls from Window in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Two women arrested following a serious incident involving a three-year-old boy who fell from a window in Rochdale have been released on bail as investigations continue.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Two women, aged 19 and 20, have been released on bail following their arrest in connection with a serious incident involving a three-year-old boy who fell from a window in Rochdale. The incident occurred on Saturday, August 22, shortly after 4.15pm, at a property on Spotland Tops in the Cutgate area.

Emergency services, including police and paramedics, responded to the scene, with an air ambulance also landing nearby. The boy was taken to hospital in a critical condition. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) have confirmed that inquiries into the circumstances surrounding the incident are ongoing.

The two women were arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child and were detained at an address in Blackburn, Lancashire, before being released on bail as investigations continue. GMP has stated that they are working to establish the full details of the incident.

As of now, there has been no update on the boy's condition from the police. Anyone with information related to this incident is encouraged to come forward.

articles.title: GCSE Results Improve for Rochdale Pupils in 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale pupils have achieved higher GCSE results this year, with significant improvements in core subjects like English and maths, according to the latest figures from Rochdale Borough Council.
articles.content_html:
More pupils across Rochdale are achieving higher grades in their GCSEs, particularly in English and maths, according to the latest results released by Rochdale Borough Council. The percentage of Year 11 students passing more than five subjects, including both core subjects, has risen to 55.2%.

In English, 56.3% of students achieved a strong pass, defined as grades 5 to 9, while in maths, 47.5% attained similar grades. Additionally, 60.6% of students passed two sciences, marking a 5.9% increase from the previous academic year. The results also show that over 70% of students (70.5%) passed additional language subjects such as French, Spanish, or German, reflecting a 17.2% increase since 2024.

Humanities subjects also saw improvements, with 52.5% of students passing geography and history, up from 48.1% in 2025. Notably, the borough's cared-for young people demonstrated significant success, with a 3% increase in the number of pupils passing their exams, including a 4% rise in English and maths results. Highlights from results day included one student achieving two grade 8s in English literature and religious education, and another securing three grade 7s in English, science, and history.

These results indicate a positive trend in educational attainment across Rochdale, suggesting that local schools are effectively supporting their students in achieving better outcomes. The council is likely to continue monitoring these trends to further enhance educational strategies and support for all pupils in the borough.

articles.title: Thunderstorm Warning Issued for Rochdale and Greater Manchester
articles.excerpt: A thunderstorm warning has been issued for Rochdale and surrounding areas, with heavy downpours expected. Residents should prepare for potential disruptions.
articles.content_html:
A thunderstorm warning has been issued for parts of Greater Manchester, including Rochdale, as heavy downpours are expected throughout the day. The warning, announced by the Met Office, covers several areas including Trafford, Stockport, Tameside, and Oldham.

The forecast indicates that residents may experience significant rainfall, which could lead to localised flooding and travel disruptions. Motorists should exercise caution and plan their journeys accordingly, as conditions may deteriorate rapidly during the storms.

The warning is in effect from today, August 25, 2026, and is expected to last into the evening. Residents are encouraged to stay updated on weather conditions and heed any advice from local authorities regarding safety measures.

As the storms approach, it is advisable for residents to secure outdoor items and prepare for possible power outages. The Met Office will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as necessary.
